B-01.title: Agree on the starting point for the next build stage
B-01.what: Pin the exact constitution, specifications, prior implementation, and maturity state that control Wave B.
B-01.why: A new development stage cannot start safely if different contributors use different sources of truth.
B-01.changes: Wave B gets a shared starting point and a record of conflicts that were resolved.
B-01.not_yet: This does not implement a scientific exam or activate a Challenge.

B-01E.title: Make development reproducible and keep retired code out
B-01E.what: Pin the development environment, make local and CI commands match, enforce which code is authoritative, and quarantine legacy executable paths.
B-01E.why: Scientific evidence is hard to trust when different machines run different environments or retired code can silently return.
B-01E.changes: Wave B gets a reproducible development substrate.
B-01E.not_yet: This does not qualify production infrastructure or revive quarantined legacy behavior.

B-01F.title: Make changes easier to deliver without weakening review
B-01F.what: Harden the pull-request, review, merge, Hub, and completion-evidence path so one bounded change can move through Carbon with less avoidable ceremony.
B-01F.why: Carbon needs fast development and exact-head review at the same time.
B-01F.changes: The project gets a repeatable delivery path with guarded merges and explicit completion evidence.
B-01F.not_yet: This does not change scientific rules, choose scientific values, or grant qualification, launch, or production authority.

B-01G.title: Test whether repetitive schema code can be generated safely
B-01G.what: Run a small proof of a future approach that generates reviewable source code without runtime reflection or broad untrusted deserialization.
B-01G.why: Some repetitive code may be automatable, but Carbon needs evidence that automation preserves exact identities and ownership boundaries.
B-01G.changes: The team gets evidence for or against a later static code-generation approach.
B-01G.not_yet: This is queued tooling work; it does not migrate current scientific domains or block the active scientific work.

B-01H.title: Coordinate bounded development without giving agents final authority
B-01H.what: Run separate Planner, Developer, and Tester roles through a deterministic controller that binds exact identities, limits context, replays authorized evidence, and hands a verified candidate to Carbon's existing delivery process.
B-01H.why: An iterative agent loop is useful only if model assertions cannot replace evidence, protected material stays outside role context, and final review and merge remain independent gates.
B-01H.changes: Carbon gains optional, resumable development tooling for bounded multi-iteration implementation work.
B-01H.not_yet: Its bounded completion does not choose B-05 scientific values, qualify any behavior, expose hidden evaluation, or create LIVE authority. The installed Codex adapter remains fail-closed unavailable.
B-01H.current_stage_plain: B-01H completed its bounded delivery predicate through PR #78. B-05 is now active; harness adapter compatibility remains a separate fail-closed infrastructure fact.

B-02A.title: Define the exact physics job
B-02A.what: Specify the physical problem, what a candidate must output, which situations the exam represents, and how test cases are selected.
B-02A.why: Every later generator, reference answer, measurement, and candidate must refer to the same scientific job.
B-02A.changes: Downstream work gets one exact authored Challenge to build against.
B-02A.not_yet: This does not choose the real production distributions, thresholds, evidence weights, or live values.

B-02B.title: Turn a submitted idea into one exact build plan
B-02B.what: Define how a participant's strategy is compiled into a deterministic, reconstructible construction plan with no silent defaults or substitutions.
B-02B.why: Carbon must rebuild what the participant actually submitted rather than a silently changed version.
B-02B.changes: Later reconstruction can consume one exact plan with known parameters and components.
B-02B.not_yet: This does not authorize arbitrary participant code or choose real catalog values.

B-02C.title: Put hard resource limits around research and reconstruction
B-02C.what: Define resource classes, ceilings, enforcement outcomes, and records that distinguish estimates, admission, observed use, and scientific evidence.
B-02C.why: Carbon must control cost and execution risk without confusing resource policy with scientific merit.
B-02C.changes: Later practice and reconstruction paths gain a fail-closed resource-policy prerequisite.
B-02C.not_yet: This does not set real hardware classes, prices, quotas, validator capacity, funding, or production enforcement.

B-03.title: Create test cases in a controlled, auditable way
B-03.what: Define the case-generation interface and implement one bounded physics fixture that records what it intended to generate, what it produced, and why a case was rejected or replaced.
B-03.why: Truth, measurements, practice, and reconstruction all need a controlled source of canonical Challenge cases.
B-03.changes: Carbon gets the case-generation seam for the first bounded Wave B fixture.
B-03.not_yet: This does not choose production sampling values, qualify the generator, define truth, or activate live behavior.

B-04.title: Define what counts as a reference answer and what happens when truth fails
B-04.what: Register the allowed source of reference answers, its applicability and uncertainty, and explicit outcomes for disagreement, timeout, divergence, or unavailability.
B-04.why: A candidate can only be judged against an adequate, registered source of truth; silent fallback would corrupt the evidence.
B-04.changes: Measurements and qualification gain an explicit truth-authority boundary.
B-04.not_yet: This does not declare one solver universally authoritative or allow an unregistered fallback.
B-04.current_stage_plain: Completed in bounded implemented-and-tested fixture-runtime scope through PR #75; scientific, security, production, and LIVE qualification remain unearned.

B-05.title: Decide how the exam measures a model
B-05.what: Define the rules that turn reference answers and model outputs into scientific measurements and a final evaluation result.
B-05.why: Having answer data is not enough. Carbon must decide in advance what to measure, where it applies, how uncertainty enters, and which failures make a candidate ineligible before ranking.
B-05.changes: The active branch now has exact measurement/evidence identity, dependence-aware uncertainty, and reconstruction-evidence policy slices whose real scientific inputs remain unresolved.
B-05.not_yet: This does not choose real scientific thresholds, qualify a Challenge, or make the current system live.
B-05.current_stage_plain: Active from PR #78's receipt. The working contract and first three bounded slices are implemented on the ticket branch; Score Pack binding remains pending, and no real scientific value is selected.

B-06.title: Assemble the evidence needed to decide whether an exam is qualified
B-06.what: Create one auditable package that brings together evidence about case generation, reference truth, measurements, uncertainty, attacks, coverage, and limitations.
B-06.why: A folder full of completed components is weaker than a traceable case that the whole exam is fit for its intended claim.
B-06.changes: Carbon gains an explicit evidence package and a fail-closed qualification state.
B-06.not_yet: A populated template or fixture evidence does not make an exam live or scientifically qualified.

B-07R.title: Set the rules for a safe researcher assistance loop
B-07R.what: Define which research-help operations Carbon may provide, who owns them, what rights apply, and how they stay separate from official submission and scoring.
B-07R.why: Research tools are useful only if they cannot score, prequalify, submit, or leak the official exam.
B-07R.changes: Wave B gains the architectural boundary for local research services.
B-07R.not_yet: This does not yet define the exact service protocol or remote networking mechanics.

B-07S.title: Define the exact research-service protocol
B-07S.what: Specify the exact operations, request and response shapes, lifecycle, errors, bounds, and local adapter that all later research-service pieces must follow.
B-07S.why: An architecture diagram is not enough to guarantee interoperable or fail-closed behavior.
B-07S.changes: Later research-service tickets get one protocol owner instead of redefining the interface themselves.
B-07S.not_yet: This does not authorize a network listener, credentials, remote quotas, official submission operations, or production service.

B-07A.title: Tell researchers which practice tools a Challenge supports
B-07A.what: Create a capability manifest and shared types so a client can discover which bounded research operations, contracts, limits, and versions apply to a Challenge.
B-07A.why: Researchers need to know what the system offers without guessing or invoking capabilities the Challenge never registered.
B-07A.changes: The research service gains one discovery layer for supported operations.
B-07A.not_yet: This cannot expose official submission/result operations or invent capabilities that were never registered.

B-07B.title: Give every research experiment a durable record
B-07B.what: Record each research task, outcome, failure, receipt, evidence class, and lineage so later tools can tell what happened and what the result may support.
B-07B.why: Practice, shared history, utility studies, and rights controls all depend on exact provenance.
B-07B.changes: Wave B gains a common record for research experiments and their history.
B-07B.not_yet: A research receipt is not an official score, ranking, qualification, or frontier event.

B-07C.title: Give researchers useful practice without showing the real exam
B-07C.what: Build mock practice tasks, rehearsal tools, and comparisons on fresh public cases.
B-07C.why: Researchers need feedback, but practice must not reveal protected cases, official mixtures, exact margins, or official ordering.
B-07C.changes: Carbon gains a bounded practice loop with aggregate feedback.
B-07C.not_yet: Practice cannot admit, reject, rank, prequalify, or submit an official candidate.

B-07D1.title: Create a stable format for shared experiment history
B-07D1.what: Define an immutable Challenge-level history package, what it estimates, how versions are stored, and how old versions can be found.
B-07D1.why: Carbon cannot safely share research history until the history has exact identity and a stable data contract.
B-07D1.changes: The system gains an immutable data model for shared prior experiment summaries.
B-07D1.not_yet: This does not publish a qualified learned prior or personalize the history for individual miners.

B-07D2.title: Test how to publish shared history without leaking the hidden exam
B-07D2.what: Build a test-only publisher and a cumulative disclosure ledger that tracks what has been released over time.
B-07D2.why: Several individually safe releases can reveal protected structure when combined, so disclosure must be controlled across time.
B-07D2.changes: Carbon gains a fail-closed test publication path and release history.
B-07D2.not_yet: This does not authorize public activation, qualified learned publication, or signing custody.

B-07D3.title: Serve the same approved history to every researcher
B-07D3.what: Implement exact current and historical retrieval and deterministic compatibility checks against the active Challenge.
B-07D3.why: Every researcher should receive the same approved Challenge-level history and predictable handling of versions.
B-07D3.changes: The research service gains a request-time history retrieval layer.
B-07D3.not_yet: This does not create personalized guidance or predict official scores, gates, ranks, or winners.

B-07E.title: Estimate resource needs without confusing an estimate with a promise
B-07E.what: Analyze a proposed plan's likely resource needs and keep estimates separate from later forecasts, quotes, admission, observed usage, and scientific evidence.
B-07E.why: Researchers and operators need cost information, but an estimate must not become a capacity commitment, price, or scientific claim.
B-07E.changes: Carbon gains a typed resource-estimation path that uses the registered resource policy.
B-07E.not_yet: This does not set prices, quotas, remote fees, capacity, or make an uncalibrated forecast claim.

B-07F.title: Connect an exact build plan to the official-shaped evaluation path
B-07F.what: Take the compiled construction plan and run it through a controlled fixture version of Carbon's existing reconstruction lifecycle.
B-07F.why: Wave B needs to prove that the authored plan can enter the evaluation path through one explicit integration point.
B-07F.changes: Carbon gains a fixture-only bridge from strategy compilation to official-shaped execution.
B-07F.not_yet: This does not run production reconstruction, arbitrary code, real training, scientific evidence, or emissions.

B-07G.title: Make sure the research-service pieces work together without gaining extra authority
B-07G.what: Compose the research operations, route each one to its named owner, and test the combined service for missing or extra behavior.
B-07G.why: Individual modules can be correct while the assembled service routes requests incorrectly or absorbs authority it does not own.
B-07G.changes: Wave B gains a final local composition and conformance layer for the research service.
B-07G.not_yet: This service does not own official submission, scientific policy, shared-history policy, or other domain-specific scientific meaning.

B-E1.title: Handle noisy or inconclusive comparisons without forcing a winner
B-E1.what: Test reproducibility and uncertainty across repeated reconstruction and evaluation, preserving dependence between cases and allowing an inconclusive result.
B-E1.why: Candidate order can change under variance. Carbon needs a way to say the evidence did not resolve the comparison.
B-E1.changes: Carbon gains a statistical evidence harness for unstable or contested outcomes.
B-E1.not_yet: Partial evidence, forecasts, screens, or heuristics cannot create a superior result.

B-E2.title: Fail safely when the reference solver cannot answer
B-E2.what: Implement explicit outcomes when a registered truth source diverges, times out, disagrees, or becomes unavailable.
B-E2.why: Carbon must preserve truth-system failures instead of silently turning them into a candidate score or switching to another source.
B-E2.changes: The exam gains fail-closed reference-failure behavior and fixtures.
B-E2.not_yet: This does not allow unregistered fallback or relabel infrastructure failure as candidate science.

B-E3.title: Trace every claim to the evidence that supports it
B-E3.what: Map each scientific or engineering claim to its supporting evidence, limitations, and the place in the evidence package where that support lives.
B-E3.why: A technically complete system can still overclaim if nobody can show which evidence supports each statement and which evidence is missing.
B-E3.changes: Carbon gains a claim-to-evidence and claim-to-limitation crosswalk.
B-E3.not_yet: A crosswalk cannot fill an evidence gap or turn design intent into qualification.

B-E4.title: Try to break the research loop before trusting it
B-E4.what: Attack the research workflow for hidden-exam leakage, poisoning, gaming, collapsed method diversity, and unsafe evidence use while also testing whether it produces useful research.
B-E4.why: A research assistant can appear to improve performance by exploiting the evaluator or narrowing search instead of producing transferable scientific improvement.
B-E4.changes: Carbon gains an adversarial test of the Wave B research loop and the claims made about its usefulness.
B-E4.not_yet: Historical fit or local improvement does not establish safe utility without the preregistered test evidence.

B-GATE.title: Prove the whole Wave B system fits together and close the wave
B-GATE.what: Run the integrated fixture workflow, check cross-domain invariants, audit for placeholders that might look live, and produce the closeout evidence.
B-GATE.why: All individual tickets can pass while the combined system violates a boundary or exposes a fixture as if it were qualified behavior.
B-GATE.changes: Carbon gains the bounded evidence needed to close Wave B and hand development to Wave C.
B-GATE.not_yet: Wave B closeout still does not create real training, live science, production service, Bittensor weights, or settlement authority.
